about: The Ordinary of the Mass a Renaissance composer sets (the owner, 15 November 2026: "We'll be setting the Ordinary of the Mass, similarly to Palestrina"; "We'll set a Kyrie and an Agnus Dei, for this project to start with"): each movement's sections as Palestrina's masses divide them (Miller's encodings: Kyrie and Kyrie II, Agnus I and Agnus II), each section's text as the liturgical books print it, accents kept, and its phrases -- each one point of imitation (latin-text.js reads them; underlay.js lays them on the notes). The Christe sets its own invocation between the Kyries; the second Agnus sets the third invocation, as his do.

tactus.about: A piece's tactus, the beat a Renaissance singer felt, drawn from the piece's seed within the period's own: the theorists "related the speed of the tactus to the speed of the pulse ... usually in the range of 60 to 80 beats per minute", "neither too slow, nor too fast", Apel's reading of them an unvarying tactus near 70 (S. A. Kingsbury 2002, "Tempo and Mensural Proportion in the Music of the Sixteenth Century", Choral Journal 42(9), April 2002; research-downloads/renaissance/kingsbury-2002-tempo, OCR'd). The meter's beat as many times faster as the tactus holds beats (mass-plan.js tactusOf): 4/2's minim two to a tactus, 3/2's three (the owner, 16 November 2026: "make sure the tempi are realistic"; RCP-002's question 9, a measured tactus).

lengths: Each movement whole in Palestrina's masses, to the nearest breve of 4/2, [breves, how many masses], by the voices of the mass (Miller's encodings, measured on the trunk on 16 November 2026 by research/renaissance-mass/movement-wholes.mjs: a mass's Kyrie is one file or several, its Agnus Dei mostly two): the length a composer draws a movement at, for the voices nearest its own that ten masses or more measure. `shares`: how the movement's length divides among its sections -- the Kyrie's in thirds (where his files divide it, nine masses of four voices, the Kyrie and Christe together a median 59 breves, the last Kyrie 31); the Agnus Dei's as his masses in two files have them (a median 38 and 43 breves).
source: The Divinum Officium project's Order of Mass, web/www/missa/Latin/Ordo/Ordo.txt (github.com/DivinumOfficium/divinum-officium at d6c80662; MIT licence, Copyright (c) 2026 Divinum Officium; the trunk's research-downloads/liturgical-texts/divinum-officium): the Kyrie its lines 76-84, the Agnus Dei its lines 299-301.
meters: Each movement's sections in Palestrina's masses by the meter they are written in (Miller's encodings, music21's corpus/palestrina: 158 Kyrie and 193 Agnus Dei sections of four to eight voices, measured on the trunk on 15 November 2026 by research/renaissance-mass/movement-sections.mjs): the meter a composer draws them in.
